ports.note: Two tables in, one out: the rows of the second under the first, columns lined up by name. Both must have the same value column and unit; a key column only one has is empty on the other's rows.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet. The receipt names how many rows came from each table and every column only one of them has.

changes.description: Columns are lined up in a grid: one row per column of the stacked table, the column of each table filling it or none, each changeable, and a stacked column renamed for every table (stackUnder). Each table is shown as read, before, and the stack after. A table holding the others' names under a column of its own is refused, naming the column to stack it under; the name most tables use is offered, whatever the order of the inputs. A run stopped there keeps the tables reaching it, so Columns can be used. A table whose value column or unit differs is named, with where to change it. The Inspector moves out of app.ts. A table whose every name matches the others' column is lined up without asking, and said in the grid and the run; Start again returns to that. "persons" and "people" are one unit. Labels take {census} and the other words from the workflow.

evidence.note: Unit tested on columns both, one and neither table hold, different value columns and units, and a source column that clashes. The Salmonella example uses it to stack 32 cases on 81 matched panel controls. Nothing here establishes that two tables are fit to be stacked. 0.2.1: tests/append-rows.test.mjs; tests/population-example-opens.browser.mjs; Chromium. 0.2.2: tests/salmonella-from-scratch.browser.mjs (the matched panel controls appended through the dialog, the sentence naming both labels); Chromium. 0.3.0: tests/table-walkthroughs.test.mjs holds the walkthrough to this step's own function under every choice it follows; tests/table-walkthroughs.browser.mjs opens it from Configure…, Chromium and WebKit.
